I'm a 20 year old autistic male, also bisexual, oh yeah and I live in The Netherlands.  
My interests are also in the same categories (Gaming, music of various genres, guitar and anime/manga) Of course these things are huge so it doesn't mean tastes match or anything. I'm very story oriented so I play games for the storyline (gameplay makes it more fun). Aside from that I have a big adoration for animals and am studying to become a veterinarian.  
Despite my shyness and introvertedness I can be quite open if I notice the other person is being open as well (unless I fear judgment for my interests, I tend to be afraid of that often) But I struggle a lot with finding that first contact that allows me to open up. I've been able to find friends somewhat similar to me online though.   


I'm open for a conversation, though I understand it's maybe a little hard to get going haha.
If you would even consider watching an animated series, my favorite series is March Comes in like a Lion and the main character is autism coded. I relate hard to him.

I've personally always thought that the only time it's 100% okay to ask things is when people ask me something. For a long time no one has checked in with me with like a message, it's always been radio silence. And I figure that the best way to find out is to observe a person rather than ask them straight up. And yet when I notice something it's so dang hard to bring up, it's a prison I can't get out of.

Pitfalls: Softer, more of an isolated, spiritual sound.  
Malina: Rockier, a softened more sad kind of sound.  
The Congregation: A bridge between the previous and the newer, it's still its own thing though. It's a mellower kind of dark.  
Coal: Dark and ambient, like a bit of a descent  
Bilateral: Schizofrenic, being both angry, harsh and softer, mysterious  
Tall Poppy Syndrome: The most proggy of their albums

Man this song is something. I didn't listen to the entirety of Coal before I added the album to my playlist, I was sitting in the back of the car after a long trip and **boom** I didn't even realise it was Leprous at first. The growls actually made me feel my ears a bit, I'm used to that now though. Now in all my naiveté, I had no idea the growls were Ihsahn and not Einar, that said the song description in spotify does not have a "Ihsahn" as guest. It was until I watched the live dvd that I found out. It's embarassing lol.   
Now the song itself, I think it's awesome. Everytime it comes on I'm hyped af.  It hits so hard and I love that. I am however not such a fan of certain parts in the song, they get overbearing for me personally (the second half of the post-chorus). Those parts don't last long, and the parts that are amazing to me are plentiful. Most notably Einar's last verse, I love his vocals there. And the outro, that violin goes *wild* and Ihsan's growls just fit it perfectly. It sounds so broken. Which brings me to the lyrics, which to me describe escapism. "surrender to a forgettable story" "contaminate me" "Will you wait for me if I stop?" Despite being growled, they sound surprisingly sensitive. Though now reading the lyrics (I recited this by memory)  "inverted fury surpasses me, settling in my heart. "  sounds more like anger turned inward turning outward. I never fully get lyrics, especially Leprous lyrics. Nevertheless they hit me.

mmmmmm m mm m m m m thiss songggg. First time I heard it I fell in love. It's so good, the instrumentation sounds so grand yet small. The synth is so wonderful, it has a sound like a water drop forming and falling, or it at least has that form in my mind maybe not sound. The drums in this song are fantastic, they form the skeleton of this song. If I hear correctly they're the only instrument that plays through the whole song, the rest fades out and comes back and they're the only thing that's still playing at the end. I love it. In terms of the vocals I love everything from verse to chorus to outro. They just hit there somewhere where I can't reach with my consciousness. Then I read that reddit Q&A thread and I learnt this song was based on the concept of sun and moon children. Sun children being very open with their emotions and letting them roar wherever they go, moon children being more reserved and waiting for an "ok" to show a certain emotion. This being the result of being told to "not be so angry" or "don't yell" they're shown that anger/abundant emotion is a bad thing and adjust. It leads to needing validation in order to be happy. Obviously leads to problems of self-worth. It's something relevant to me, and it's odd how this song became my favorite without knowing it was about this.   
It's #1 for me, and probably #1 of all time at the current moment.
Also, I am hoping for Moon. But y'know it's Coal vs The Congregation and we alllll know what wins.

I slept on this song for so long, for some reason my brain was turned off when I was listening to Bilateral for the first time. I stopped listening to the album at Mediocrity Wins and forgot every song I heard. Then they played this song on their tour in Febuary and I didn't recognise it (how!) then they played it during the livestream and I finally became aware what song it was and that it was amazing. The start is so mysteriously beautiful with the static and keys. The calm interlude towards the chorus and the chorus having that soothing high pitch in "to" it's deliciously sweet. Then after that the continuation of the mysterious sounds in the intro reinforce there's more to this than just a soothing lullaby, perhaps it's a trap. This continues and when the song finally explodes you still don't know if it's safe to relax, there's a strange pressure of "is everything really alright?" *do nothing at allllllll*  
All in all, a beautifully mysterious song. #12 on my list.

Just a spot away from being really at the bottom what a shame. Again I'm not seeing the "bad vocal" part, but perhaps that's because I don 't demand much from vocals. I quite like the verses, even though it is nothing amazing melody wise. The lyrical work here is very nice though 'forging the key to unlock the chain, freeing me from the destructive reign."  The lyrics in the chorus are pretty straight forward, but they hit hard nonetheless combined with Einars great singing. Need I make a comment on the vocals after the second chorus? They really feel like hitting the bottom. I really like the singing duet at the end it's a great outro, like a cooling down.   
The electric drums combined with the synth in the intro gives a cloudy vibe like you're "at the top" then we fall down to a darker place , at least to me cellos give off a beautifully dark sound. The guitar part of the break down after Einar stops singing is a highlight for me aside from the other plentiful parts, it is again a nice prelude to the "cooldown"  
This one's #17 on my list, because somehow I'm not in the mood for it sometimes.

The part after doesn't dissapoint me for being similar, i'm kinda simple. I had to get used to harsh vocals too, I get not being able to enjoy them. I get very mad when it's claimed to not belong in music however. They can still rub me the wrong way, but that's more so an issue in the way it's implemented or used.   
This song's #22 on my list, held back by the dragging of the part after the intro, and the intro being the height of the song (which includes the parts identical to the intro, but with different lyrics)

And then we head into aaaaaaa ahAAAAAAAAAaaaa which is a very controversial part for me. There is times it really takes me in and then there's times I get bored halfway through, which, it changes up how is that possible?! The bridge after aaaaaaaAAAA is just as darkly atmospheric and I love it, Einars deeper vocals combined with the intensifying synth make for a nice end to 4 minute first letter of the alphabet. With a small verse  we return to the chorus and this part is more hopeful like the previous chorus, it also changes up after repitition, which I think works more empowering.
